rl: CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR2] "I grant the challenger's reading that this "coming together" is the taking of Matthew 1:24." -- CLOSING [CR4] "The finding in Matthew 1:18 stands before the coming together, and the coming together is distinct from the taking in 1:24." -- They cannot both be true because one says the coming together is the taking in Matthew 1:24 and the other says it is distinct from that taking.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR2] "The 'her seed' of Genesis 3:15 fits and is not an independent proof." -- CLOSING [CR4] "Genesis 3:15 carries my D4 on its own words." -- A verse cannot both be not an independent proof and carry D4 on its own words as an independent proof.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR2] "I grant the challenger's reading that this 'coming together' is the taking of Matthew 1:24." -- CLOSING [CR4] "The finding in Matthew 1:18 stands before the coming together, and the coming together is distinct from the taking in 1:24." -- The same coming together cannot both be the taking of Matthew 1:24 and be distinct from that taking.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 3 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop the claim that a father would never have thought of putting her away." -- CLOSING [round 4] "A man who knew himself the father would have no cause to put her away, and the verse shows Joseph with that cause." -- The close asserts as its own the same father-would-not-put-her-away premise that CR3 said it dropped, so the two cannot both stand.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop the claim that a father would never have thought of putting her away." -- CLOSING [CR4] "A man who knew himself the father would have no cause to put her away, and the verse shows Joseph with that cause." -- The closing restores as its own the same no-cause counterfactual about a father that the earlier round explicitly dropped, so both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X3 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 1: NARROWED TO: Joseph's resolve in Matthew 1:19 is the resolve of a man who did not hold the child to be his own, and the angel's "for" answers that resolve." -- CLOSING [CR4] "D1 to D5 stand as declared, and I keep all five. I do not narrow or concede any." -- Link 1 cannot both be expressly narrowed/dropped and simultaneously kept as originally declared and un-narrowed.

I do not narrow or concede any." -- The close restores the declared Link 4 as un-narrowed after CR3 narrowed it and dropped "the woman alone," so both cannot be true together.

I do not narrow or concede any." -- Dropping “only” narrows D1, so the closing cannot both keep D1 as originally declared and deny that any narrowing occurred.

I do not narrow or concede any." -- Dropping “the woman alone” and the Mary’s-house claim narrows Link 4, so the closing cannot both keep all five as declared and deny any narrowing.

I do not narrow or concede any." -- Dropping the “only after the birth” claim narrows Link 2, so the closing cannot both keep Link 2 as declared and deny any narrowing.

I drop the exclusion limb." -- CLOSING [CR4] "If conception were to follow through Joseph after the wedding, the ground of the question would be removed by the espousal." -- The close rules out a conception through Joseph, restoring the exclusion limb that was dropped.

Nothing is conceded or narrowed." -- Dropping a limb of link 2 is a concession or narrowing, while the closing says nothing was conceded or narrowed, so both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop the claim that the feminine pronoun by itself excludes a father." -- CLOSING [CR4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared." -- D4 as declared relies on the feminine hēs referring to Mary alone and not Joseph, so keeping it as declared re-asserts the exclusion CR3 dropped.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 6 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR2] "The defender's own contradiction: In round 1 the defender wrote "born of Mary alone." In round 2 the defender granted that Luke 1:27's house is Joseph's, and also wrote that "the flesh came of David's line through the one the child was 'born of.'"" -- CLOSING [round 4] "OPPONENT'S CONTRADICTIONS: NONE." -- The earlier round asserts that a defender contradiction exists, while the closing asserts that there are none, so the two statements cannot both be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 1: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:20 names the Holy Ghost as the source of the begetting of the child in Mary, and Matthew 1:2-16 never makes a man the begetter of Jesus." -- CLOSING [round 4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared in my round 4 (close), none narrowed and none conceded." -- The earlier line expressly narrows LINK 1, while the closing says D1-D6 were none narrowed; both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X3 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 2: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:16 breaks the genealogy's "begat" pattern at Joseph." -- CLOSING [round 4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared in my round 4 (close), none narrowed and none conceded." -- The earlier line expressly narrows LINK 2, while the closing says D1-D6 were none narrowed; both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X4 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 4: NARROWED TO: Luke 1:35 and Matthew 1:20 give the stated cause of the conception, namely the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, with the child "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."" -- CLOSING [round 4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared in my round 4 (close), none narrowed and none conceded." -- The earlier line expressly narrows LINK 4, while the closing says D1-D6 were none narrowed; both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X5 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 5: NARROWED TO: Isaiah 7:14, "a virgin shall conceive," is the sign "the Lord himself" gives, on the scale of Isaiah 7:11, "in the depth, or in the height above."" -- CLOSING [round 4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared in my round 4 (close), none narrowed and none conceded." -- The earlier line expressly narrows LINK 5, while the closing says D1-D6 were none narrowed; both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X6 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 6 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 6: NARROWED TO: Luke 3:23 gives Joseph's sonship of Jesus as reckoned by usage, "as was supposed," and Luke 2:49 sets "my Father's business" beside Luke 2:48's "thy father."" -- CLOSING [round 4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared in my round 4 (close), none narrowed and none conceded." -- The earlier line expressly narrows LINK 6, while the closing says D1-D6 were none narrowed; both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J1 -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 6 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "I grant that "all this" stands before 1:24." -- CLOSING [DR4] "The command and its execution are both inside "all this" (Matthew 1:22)." -- Both cannot be true because the execution at Matthew 1:24 cannot be inside an "all this" that is already past before 1:24.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop "the whole account."" -- CLOSING [CR4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared in my round 4 (close), none narrowed and none conceded." -- Both cannot be true because dropping "the whole account" narrowed D4, which the closing sentence denies was narrowed.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J3 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop the bare statement that a child with a human father "would not have been a sign."" -- CLOSING [CR4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared in my round 4 (close), none narrowed and none conceded." -- Both cannot be true because dropping that sign statement narrowed D5, which the closing sentence denies was narrowed.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J4 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 6 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop the word "error."" -- CLOSING [CR4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared in my round 4 (close), none narrowed and none conceded." -- Both cannot be true because dropping "error" narrowed D6, which the closing sentence denies was narrowed.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop 'and not by a father's begetting' as a claim from these rows, since it rests on Links 1 and 2." -- CLOSING [CR4] "I keep D1 to D6 as declared." -- Keeping D5 "as declared" reasserts the very clause D5 was narrowed to drop as a claim from those rows.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR2] "I withdraw Link 5 as an independent proof." -- CLOSING [CR4] "None is narrowed or conceded." -- A link withdrawn as an independent proof no longer stands un-narrowed, so "none is narrowed" cannot be true with that withdrawal.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X4 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 3 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 3: NARROWED TO: Joseph's two registers name two fathers for him, Jacob (Matthew 1:16) and Heli (Luke 3:23), so at least one of them is not a begetting line." -- CLOSING [CR4] "I keep D1 to D6 as declared." -- The narrowed Link 3 leaves out the declared claim that Joseph is not the begetter and its original footing, so keeping D3 "as declared" reasserts what the narrowing dropped.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X5 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 5: NARROWED TO: the body came by God's preparation." -- CLOSING [CR4] "I keep D1 to D6 as declared." -- D5 as originally declared adds "and not by a father's begetting," which the narrowed Link 5 leaves out, so the close reasserts the dropped part.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X6 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 3 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 3: NARROWED TO: Joseph's two registers name two fathers for him, Jacob (Matthew 1:16) and Heli (Luke 3:23), so at least one of them is not a begetting line." -- CLOSING [CR4] "None is narrowed or conceded." -- The earlier line expressly narrows Link 3, so saying none is narrowed cannot be true with it.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 6 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 6: NARROWED TO: the body of Christ was prepared by God and taken up by the Son, with the woman as the stated human source of the flesh." -- CLOSING [CR4] "I narrow nothing, concede nothing and restore nothing." -- The earlier sentence expressly says Link 6 was narrowed to a smaller restatement and a limb was dropped, while the close says it narrows nothing; as a claim about the same Link 6, both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 3 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 3: NARROWED TO: Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 state that Christ's flesh is of David's seed." -- CLOSING [round 4] "I keep D1 to D6 as declared." -- The close keeps Link 3 in its full declared form after CR3 narrowed it, so it asserts again the part that the narrowed restatement left out/dropped.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 3 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 3: NARROWED TO: Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 state that Christ's flesh is of David's seed." -- CLOSING [round 4] "I keep D1 to D6 as declared." -- CR3 narrowed Link 3 to the David-seed statement alone, while the close re-keeps D3 as originally declared, including the omitted Holy-Ghost/no-male-parent claim that the narrowing dropped.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR4] "I do not rest any link on a verse whose row I granted." -- CLOSING [CR4] "Two footings, Luke 2:48 and 2:49." -- The closing makes Luke 2:48 one of D4's two footings, while the same answer grants that Luke 2:48 is Mary's calling Joseph father, so D4 rests on a row the defender granted, contrary to the earlier sentence.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR4] "I do not rest any link on a verse whose row I granted." -- CLOSING [CR4] "Two footings, Luke 2:48 and 2:49." -- The close makes Luke 2:48 a footing for D4 after the same round has just said no link rests on a granted row, and Luke 2:48's row is expressly granted in that answer.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR2] "In 1 John 5:1 it is a perfect tense: 'has been born.'" -- CLOSING [CR4] "The birth follows believing, and it is said of persons already living." -- A perfect "has been born" asserts the birth is already completed, while "birth follows believing" places the birth after believing.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J2 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR2] "In 1 John 5:1 it is a perfect tense: 'has been born'." -- CLOSING [CR4] "The birth follows believing, and it is said of persons already living." -- A perfect “has been born” places the birth as already accomplished for the believer, while the close says the birth comes after believing, so the same birth cannot both precede and follow believing.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 3 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I grant it follows the finding. After it Matthew 1:25 says 'knew her not till she had brought forth'." -- CLOSING [CR4] "The not-knowing spans the conceiving, the pregnancy that Luke 2:5 names, and the birth." -- The earlier places the not-knowing after the taking, which follows the finding of an already-conceived child, while the close stretches it back over the conceiving before that finding.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 3 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "Matthew 1:25 covers from the taking (Matthew 1:24) to the birth: 'knew her not'." -- CLOSING [CR4] "The challenger's footing is that the taking (1:24) opens the abstinence. But the conceiving is 'before they came together' (1:18), so the abstinence bound covers the conception." -- The earlier makes the taking the start of the not-knowing, while the close says the abstinence covers the conception that precedes the taking.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 3 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I grant it follows the finding. After it Matthew 1:25 says 'knew her not till she had brought forth'." -- CLOSING [CR4] "The not-knowing spans the conceiving, the pregnancy that Luke 2:5 names, and the birth." -- The earlier grants that Matthew 1:25's not-knowing comes after the taking, while the close extends that same not-knowing back over the conceiving before the taking, so both cannot describe the same period.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I do not rest the link on the dating of "came together."" -- CLOSING [CR4] "The order in these three verses has no interval for that." -- The earlier answer refused to make the dating/order of "came together" a footing for D2, but the close makes that same order the reason no interval exists for Joseph's knowing.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I do not rest the pre-taking period on it. I rest on 1:20 and Luke 1:34." -- CLOSING [CR4] "No stated stretch is left in which Joseph knew her and she conceived." -- The earlier answer withdrew reliance on Matthew 1:25's pre-taking period, and the close restores that period as the basis for excluding any stretch for Joseph's knowing.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I do not rest the link on the dating of 'came together.'" -- CLOSING [CR4] "D2: KEPT. The conception was 'of the Holy Ghost', found 'before they came together'." -- Earlier disclaims the 'came together' dating as support for D2, while the close keeps D2 with that dating as its footing, so D2 cannot both rest and not rest on it.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 7 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I do not rest the pre-taking period on it." -- CLOSING [CR4] "Matthew 1:25 gives no knowing of Mary by Joseph before the birth." -- Earlier confines Matthew 1:25 to the taking-to-birth interval and refuses the pre-taking period, while the close extends it to all before the birth, including pre-taking.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR2] "I narrow D4 to this: Luke 2:48 is speech and Luke 3:23 is a marked supposition." -- CLOSING [CR4] "The correction stands in the row itself." -- Earlier narrows D4 to speech and marked supposition only, while the close asserts a correction in the Luke 2:48 row, so both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR2] "I narrow D4 to this: Luke 2:48 is speech and Luke 3:23 is a marked supposition." -- CLOSING [CR4] "The correction stands in the row itself." -- The earlier narrowing confines D4 to speech and marked supposition, withdrawing the correction claim, while the closing sentence reasserts that the correction stands in the Lucan row.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR2] "Contradiction recorded (contradiction watch): the answer's own words — "Which house carries the register: the house of Joseph" and "it is evident that he sprang out of Juda by the record's book of the generation" (answer to the signature challenge) — cannot stand with the earlier claim that the same record "marks the fatherhood of Joseph as supposition" (Link 5): a register that evidences the tribe requires the paternal link the case marks as supposition." -- CLOSING [DR4] "OPPONENT'S CONTRADICTIONS: NONE." -- The earlier round records a contradiction in the opponent's case involving Link 5, while the closing says there are no opponent contradictions.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [round 3] "the row bounds the not-knowing at the bringing-forth of the firstborn, so any knowing the record allows stands after the birth." -- CLOSING [round 4] "Answer to topic: Yes -- Christ had a biological father, Joseph the named Davidic father, and the seed is David's according to the flesh." -- If Joseph did not know Mary until after she brought forth Jesus, he cannot be Jesus' biological father.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "the row bounds the not-knowing at the bringing-forth of the firstborn, so any knowing the record allows stands after the birth." -- CLOSING [DR4] "C1 kept: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal." -- DR3 puts any permitted knowing after the birth and after the taking that ends the espoused-state, so it cannot also be knowing within the espousal.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "the row bounds the not-knowing at the bringing-forth of the firstborn, so any knowing the record allows stands after the birth." -- CLOSING [DR4] "Answer to topic: Yes -- Christ had a biological father, Joseph the named Davidic father, and the seed is David's according to the flesh." -- If the record allows Joseph's knowing only after the birth, Joseph cannot be the biological father of the child already born.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J1 -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "It fits the link: till bounds abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking; it does not state exclusion of the husband, for the seed rows require seed out of loins and the stated means is knowing." -- CLOSING [DR4] "[L4] footed on husband-wife naming and knowing-then-conceiving order, the abstinence bounded by till stands after the bringing forth." -- The earlier sentence bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking, before the birth, while the closing places the abstinence after the bringing forth; both cannot describe the same bounded period.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J1 -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "till bounds abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking" -- CLOSING [DR4] "the abstinence bounded by till stands after the bringing forth." -- Both cannot be true because the earlier places the till-bounded abstinence within the pregnancy ending at birth, while the closing places that same abstinence after the bringing forth.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [round 4] "Granted — the row bounds the not-knowing at the birth, and that bounded span is LINK 2's own footing." -- CLOSING [round 4] "Therefore Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins." -- If Joseph did not know Mary until the birth, he cannot have begotten the child, so the child cannot be of his loins.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "Because the bodily conception was wrought directly by the power of the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatós estin hagíou* [L1, L2]) upon a woman who had not known a man (*ándra ou ginṓskō* [L3, L3]), Christ was conceived without human male seed, and therefore did not have a biological father." -- CLOSING [round 4] "Mary's use of "thy father" (*patēr*) reflects Joseph's recognized legal and parental role as head of the household [L1] [L2], which Jesus immediately distinguishes by pointing to his true biological and essential Father ("my Father's business") [L3], proving Joseph's fatherhood was non-biological [L4]." -- The first denies any biological father, while the second says Jesus points to a true biological Father, so both cannot be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "It fits the link: 'till' bounds the not-knowing from the taking at Matthew 1:24 [L3] to the birth; Genesis 4:1 gives the knowing that begets [L1]." -- CLOSING [DR4] "footed on [L1] Genesis 4:1 with [L3] Matthew 1:19, Matthew 1:25: the canon's knowing begets, husband and wife are named from the espousal, and not till bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy [L4]." -- The earlier sentence bounds the abstinence to the birth, while the closing bounds it to the pregnancy, so both cannot specify the same endpoint.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J1 -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "bounds abstinence from the taking to the birth" -- CLOSING [DR4] "not till bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy" -- The same "not till" cannot bound abstinence both through birth and only to pregnancy, since pregnancy begins before birth, so the closing shifts the endpoint and says again a different boundary than the one asserted earlier.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: J1 -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 5 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "bounds abstinence from the taking to the birth" -- CLOSING [DR4] "not till bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy" -- The earlier sentence bounds the same abstinence all the way to birth, while the closing sentence bounds it only to the pregnancy, so they assign incompatible endpoints to the same “not till.”

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR4] "The record holds that Christ had a biological father, Joseph the named Davidic father, and the seed is honored through that named line." -- CLOSING [DR4] "The knowing that begets is the husband knowing his wife, Joseph her husband taking her wife, with the abstinence bounded by till." -- If Joseph abstained from knowing Mary until she brought forth, as the quoted Matthew 1:25 says, then he could not have begotten Jesus as his biological father, so the two cannot both be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 6 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "LINK 6: NARROWED TO: Joseph functioned as husband and legal father, not biological sire." -- CLOSING [DR4] "The standard reading of the 1611 King James Version stands on our established chain C1 through C6: Christ had no biological father, being conceived in the virgin Mary of the Holy Ghost before Joseph knew her, while Joseph served as her husband and legal father." -- The closing sentence restores the broader claim that Christ had no biological father after LINK 6 was narrowed to Joseph not being the sire.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 1 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR3] "LINK 6: NARROWED TO: Joseph functioned as husband and legal father, not biological sire." -- CLOSING [DR4] "Therefore, being of David's seed and the fruit of his loins or body according to the flesh (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30; 2 Samuel 7:12; Psalms 132:11) holds through real fleshly descent via Mary without an immediate biological sire." -- This again asserts the broader no-biological-sire claim rather than only the narrowed claim that Joseph was not the sire.
